CONTENT: 01 - Confirm parser scope and scheduling requirements
Inventory supported and disabled parser configurations
DESCRIPTION: Current runner dispatches Endfield, Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero sequentially. Wuthering Waves is commented out; FGO/GF2/NTE configurations do not represent working integrations.

CONTENT: Choose the initial games to schedule
DESCRIPTION: Enable only implemented, validated games. Treat Wuthering Waves activation and missing integrations as separate reviewed work; do not create jobs merely because a configuration file exists.

CONTENT: Choose one scheduler for the NAS
DESCRIPTION: Prefer DSM Task Scheduler user-defined scripts. Use cron only if deliberately supported and maintained; do not duplicate the same jobs in DSM and crontab.

CONTENT: Define source-refresh frequency and freshness targets
DESCRIPTION: Choose a conservative polling cadence based on source terms, runtime and acceptable staleness. Source scraping frequency is separate from daily/weekly/monthly activity reset rules.

CONTENT: Record NAS timezone and game-server reset profiles
DESCRIPTION: Document each supported server timezone, reset instant and DST behavior. Do not treat NAS local midnight as the reset for every game.

CONTENT: Choose one all-games job or implement explicit game selection
DESCRIPTION: The current npm run parser:start executes the sequential runner and has no per-game CLI filter. Start with one locked job, or add and test game/source selectors before defining separate schedules.

CONTENT: Gate: approve the enabled games and scheduling policy
DESCRIPTION: Record scheduler owner, allowed sources, cadence, timezone assumptions and expected completion/freshness thresholds. Do not invent production schedules until these are selected.

CONTENT: 02 - Make the runner safe for unattended execution
Validate configurations before opening database or browser clients
DESCRIPTION: Validate JSON shape, enabled IDs and source types. Distinguish disabled/planned placeholders from invalid enabled configurations; handle malformed files without misleading success.

CONTENT: Return a failing process exit code for failed enabled parsers
DESCRIPTION: The current per-game catch logs errors and continues. Aggregate failures into a nonzero final outcome while retaining per-game/source diagnostics.

CONTENT: Distinguish successful empty results from extraction failures
DESCRIPTION: Do not swallow source exceptions as empty arrays. Record structured source outcomes and preserve last successful data when extraction fails.

CONTENT: Await database initialization and guarantee disconnection
DESCRIPTION: Replace constructor-started connection side effects with awaited lifecycle ownership. Close MongoDB in finally paths on success, errors and cancellation.

CONTENT: Make headless mode configurable for NAS execution
DESCRIPTION: The shared parser currently hardcodes headless=false. Verify Chromium can run without an interactive desktop and retain the browser sandbox where supported.

CONTENT: Guarantee browser cleanup and bounded source processing
DESCRIPTION: Close pages and browsers in finally paths; configure navigation/readiness timeouts and bounded retries with backoff. Replace unconditional fixed waits with tested readiness checks.

CONTENT: Handle SIGTERM and interrupted runs
DESCRIPTION: Stop accepting new work, close browser/DB resources and exit within a bounded grace period. Forced termination must not leave a partially destructive refresh.

CONTENT: Add run and source outcome summaries
DESCRIPTION: Include run ID, game/source, start/end, duration, counts and error category. Report actual success, partial failure, timeout and intentional skip distinctly.

CONTENT: Gate: demonstrate bounded execution and accurate failure status
DESCRIPTION: Verify success exits zero, enabled-source failures exit nonzero, cleanup occurs and the process terminates without hanging.

CONTENT: 03 - Protect existing data and completion tracking
Move destructive cleanup after validated source acquisition
DESCRIPTION: Do not delete catalog records before fetching their replacements. Preserve last successful records on timeout, invalid markup or empty-failure results.

CONTENT: Preserve ended event history and manually added content
DESCRIPTION: Use an explicit retention/archive policy. Never broadly remove same-title records or user/editor-managed entries.

CONTENT: Use stable activity and occurrence identities for upserts
DESCRIPTION: Allow date/URL corrections without changing personal completion identity. Preserve progress mappings through additive migration or aliases.

CONTENT: Align expiry and recurrence semantics with the UI
DESCRIPTION: Test the full end day, end-exclusive instants, timezone boundaries and recurring periods. Verify Genshin 1st/16th monthly cycles without duplicating or losing occurrences.

CONTENT: Avoid no-op revision changes and unsafe concurrent writes
DESCRIPTION: Advance shared revisions only on real changes. Make deduplication/upserts atomic and ensure API/editor changes cannot be overwritten by stale parser snapshots.

CONTENT: Verify parser writes cannot reset personal user state
DESCRIPTION: Parser output updates shared definitions only. Preserve account completion, collection data and editor content.

CONTENT: Test repeated runs and source corrections for idempotency
DESCRIPTION: Run the same fixtures twice; confirm no duplicate records, unnecessary revision churn or changed completion keys. Test corrected dates and overlapping same-name cycles.

CONTENT: Gate: prove failure and reruns preserve production-equivalent data
DESCRIPTION: Use disposable data to verify history, manual records and user progress survive failed fetches, retries, cancellations and successful reruns.

CONTENT: 04 - Package the parser runtime and NAS configuration
Build a versioned Linux AMD64 parser image
DESCRIPTION: Reuse the deployment plan's immutable tested releases. Include the required runtime/shared modules; do not depend on omitted development-only tsx packages.

CONTENT: Install and verify Chromium runtime dependencies
DESCRIPTION: Test browser launch on DSM under the intended non-root user, sandbox settings and resource limits. Do not assume Ubuntu CI dependencies transfer unchanged.

CONTENT: Define explicit working and configuration paths
DESCRIPTION: The current runner resolves projects/data-parser/config from process.cwd(). Package that layout or add a configurable absolute config path; test the scheduled working directory.

CONTENT: Create a least-privilege parser MongoDB user
DESCRIPTION: Grant only the required application-data access. Keep administrator and private account-progress credentials out of parser configuration.

CONTENT: Store parser secrets in protected NAS configuration
DESCRIPTION: Provide DB_CONN_STRING, DB_NAME and DB_COLLECTION through the reviewed runtime contract. Do not place passwords or URIs in scheduler commands, Git, logs or Todoist.

CONTENT: Configure private database networking and outbound source access
DESCRIPTION: Use the MongoDB container alias and internal port when co-located. Allow source/DNS/TLS egress without publishing parser or database ports.

CONTENT: Set writable temporary paths and resource limits
DESCRIPTION: Provide per-run browser profiles and required cache/temp mounts only. Bound CPU, memory, PID usage and log storage; avoid broad NAS mounts.

CONTENT: Gate: run the exact parser image successfully in a disposable environment
DESCRIPTION: Verify config resolution, browser launch, database permissions, clean exit and state preservation using the intended container command.

CONTENT: 05 - Create a guarded job wrapper
Create one reviewed parser-job entry point on the NAS
DESCRIPTION: Use absolute executable, Compose/project and log paths. Scheduler execution must not rely on an interactive shell profile, npm PATH or a development PC.

CONTENT: Launch a one-shot container and propagate its exit status
DESCRIPTION: Use the reviewed Compose one-shot equivalent after verifying DSM tooling. Do not require an always-running parser container or hide failure behind a logging pipeline.

CONTENT: Prevent overlapping scheduled and manual runs
DESCRIPTION: Use an exclusive lock in a verified persistent location. Hold it for the entire child-process lifetime and record intentional overlap skips distinctly.

CONTENT: Coordinate parser jobs with deployment and backup maintenance
DESCRIPTION: Use the same maintenance/locking contract as the NAS deploy task. Stop and drain running writers before backup/migration; blocked launches must not bypass maintenance.

CONTENT: Add a maximum runtime and graceful stop policy
DESCRIPTION: Stop the entire job container/process tree after the approved deadline, then verify browser and DB cleanup. Test lock release; do not leave orphan writers.

CONTENT: Add bounded transient-error retries
DESCRIPTION: Retry only known temporary network/rate-limit failures with backoff and a cap. Do not blindly rerun destructive or invalid-configuration failures.

CONTENT: Capture redacted logs and final job status
DESCRIPTION: Keep start/end, duration, image digest, per-source outcomes and final code. Rotate logs and preserve the original failure when notification/logging also fails.

CONTENT: Add a safe manual run and disable procedure
DESCRIPTION: Manual execution uses the same lock and credentials as scheduled runs. Document how to disable future runs and stop an active job safely.

CONTENT: Gate: test overlap, timeout and maintenance behavior
DESCRIPTION: Two launches must not produce concurrent writers; timeout must stop the whole job; maintenance must block both scheduled and manual starts.

CONTENT: 06 - Configure DSM schedules without enabling production writes
Verify the DSM version and Task Scheduler capabilities
DESCRIPTION: Use Control Panel > Task Scheduler > Create > Scheduled Task > User-defined script. Confirm actual installed UI/tooling and keep the first task disabled.

CONTENT: Choose the scheduler execution identity and permissions
DESCRIPTION: Use the least privilege supported by the container launcher. Docker access is effectively administrative; protect wrapper and environment files against untrusted modification.

CONTENT: Register the reviewed wrapper with explicit paths
DESCRIPTION: Do not embed secrets, npm installs, builds or downloaded shell payloads in the task. The wrapper launches the approved parser image.

CONTENT: Configure the selected refresh times and timezone
DESCRIPTION: Use the approved cadence; stagger separate jobs only after per-game selection exists. Check DST and reboot behavior instead of assuming every missed run is replayed.

CONTENT: Configure failure notifications and log retention
DESCRIPTION: Send useful non-secret failure details. Treat intentional maintenance/overlap skips separately from errors and alert if skips cause stale data.

CONTENT: Export or document the scheduler configuration
DESCRIPTION: Record task names, script paths, account, timezone, schedule, enabled status, timeout and owner outside the NAS for recovery.

CONTENT: Gate: confirm there is one disabled scheduler configuration
DESCRIPTION: No duplicate cron/DSM jobs, unsupported game jobs, public endpoints or staging environment are required. Do not enable unattended production writes yet.

CONTENT: 07 - Verify scheduled behavior against disposable data
Run lint, parser tests and applicable regression suites
DESCRIPTION: Verify the candidate commit before publishing. Add coverage for lifecycle, failure status, config validation, date boundaries and persistence changes.

CONTENT: Test the scheduled command in a minimal environment
DESCRIPTION: Use the same working directory, user permissions, paths and environment contract as DSM; confirm no interactive login is needed.

CONTENT: Exercise source, browser and database failure scenarios
DESCRIPTION: Test unreachable sources, changed markup, invalid config, expired/invalid TLS, denied DB access and browser launch failure. Verify bounded failure with useful logs.

CONTENT: Test persistence and failure recovery using disposable MongoDB
DESCRIPTION: Use fixtures plus manual records and multiple users' progress. Confirm reruns, expiry and interrupted writes preserve intended state; never point destructive tests at production.

CONTENT: Verify notifications and stale-source detection
DESCRIPTION: Simulate partial failure, timeout and skipped runs. A job that starts regularly but fails to refresh a required source must still alert.

CONTENT: Test reboot, missed-run and deployment coordination behavior
DESCRIPTION: Verify lock recovery, task persistence, maintenance exclusions and the documented manual catch-up policy without overlapping writers.

CONTENT: Measure resource use and worst-case runtime
DESCRIPTION: Check memory/CPU/temp disk and source request volume. Adjust limits, cadence and timeouts based on measured results.

CONTENT: Gate: approve the tested image and job wrapper for first live execution
DESCRIPTION: Require passing failure-path tests, trustworthy exit codes, no data-loss regressions and recoverable configuration.

CONTENT: 08 - Enable controlled production runs and monitoring
Back up the production database and record the parser release
DESCRIPTION: Use the NAS backup/maintenance procedure; include assets if the parser gains asset writes. Preserve the previous image digest and a tested restore path.

CONTENT: Run the first controlled parser refresh through the wrapper
DESCRIPTION: Keep unattended scheduling disabled. Use a maintenance window where appropriate and inspect the actual source outcomes and changed records.

CONTENT: Check the dashboard and game events after refreshing the UI
DESCRIPTION: Verify counts, dates, urgency order, filters, artwork fallback and completion state. Existing open pages do not automatically subscribe to parser database changes.

CONTENT: Enable only the approved production schedule
DESCRIPTION: Start conservatively with the validated games and cadence. If separate game jobs are needed, enable selectors first and stagger without overlapping writes.

CONTENT: Monitor the first scheduled cycles and source freshness
DESCRIPTION: Verify duration, failures, retries, revisions, storage growth and last successful refresh per required source; tune cadence from observed behavior.

CONTENT: Verify parser jobs pause and resume safely around releases
DESCRIPTION: Coordinate image updates and database schema compatibility with the deployment maintenance lock; do not replace an image underneath a running job.

CONTENT: Document the incident and rollback procedure
DESCRIPTION: Disable the schedule, stop active writers safely and preserve logs. Revert parser images only if schema-compatible; deliberate data restoration must account for writes since backup.

CONTENT: Assign ongoing ownership for schedules and source changes
DESCRIPTION: Review freshness alerts, source policy, selectors, dependency/browser patches, credentials and recovery periodically. Choose recurring dates after agreeing operational cadence.

CONTENT: Gate: confirm unattended parser operation is reliable
DESCRIPTION: One scheduler launches tested bounded jobs, production state and progress are preserved, stale/failed sources alert and disable/recovery steps work.
